summary.minimization_hint: Use only literal BIGINT UNSIGNED constants in GREATEST/LEAST; avoid column access in failing case.
summary.notes: The bug is isolated to column-based evaluation: the literal and CASTed variants work correctly, but when arguments come from BIGINT UNSIGNED columns, ordering is inverted — suggests internal comparison function misapplies sort order (e.g., uses LEAST comparator for GREATEST or vice versa) only when reading from columns.

cases.reason: GREATEST returned 9223372036854775808 (2^63) and LEAST returned 9223372036854775807 (2^63-1), matching expected behavior. TiDB correctly handles unsigned 64-bit integers in GREATEST/LEAST without overflow/truncation.

Expected GREATEST=9223372036854775808 and LEAST=9223372036854775807, but TiDB returned GREATEST=9223372036854775807 and LEAST=9223372036854775808 — exactly reversed. This indicates a bug in columnar BIGINT UNSIGNED comparison logic in GREATEST/LEAST (possibly due to misordered arguments or signed comparison being used internally).
cases.report_draft: In GREATEST/LEAST expressions on BIGINT UNSIGNED columns, TiDB incorrectly swaps the result values — returns GREATEST as the smaller value and LEAST as the larger. Regression likely in column-based argument handling vs literal handling.

cases.reason: GREATEST correctly returned 9223372036854775808 and LEAST returned 9223372036854775807. TiDB properly handles mixed SIGNED/UNSIGNED casting in GREATEST/LEAST, suggesting the core arithmetic logic works when operands are not column references.
